blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how a compiler ensures that a variable is declared before it's used, or how it checks that the types in an expression are compatible? This is where attribute grammars and semantic rules come into play.

blocks.markdown: In the process of compiling a program, syntax analysis ensures that the source code follows the grammatical structure of the language. However, syntax alone cannot verify if the program is semantically correct, such as ensuring variables are declared before use or types are compatible in expressions. This is where semantic analysis, specifically through attribute grammars and semantic rules, becomes essential.

blocks.title: Attribute Grammars
blocks.text: An attribute grammar is a formal way to define attributes for the symbols in a grammar and rules for computing these attributes. Attributes can be synthesized or inherited.

blocks.markdown: Attributes in a grammar can be of two types: synthesized and inherited. Synthesized attributes are computed from the attributes of the children nodes in the parse tree, while inherited attributes are computed from the attributes of the parent and/or sibling nodes.

blocks.title: Synthesized Attributes
blocks.text: Synthesized attributes are those whose values are defined in terms of the attribute values of their children nodes in the parse tree.

blocks.title: Inherited Attributes
blocks.text: Inherited attributes are those whose values are defined in terms of the attribute values of their parent or sibling nodes in the parse tree.

blocks.title: Example of Synthesized Attribute
blocks.prompt: Consider the production rule for an arithmetic expression: $E \rightarrow E_1 + T$. Define a synthesized attribute for computing the value of the expression.

steps.text: Define the semantic rule for $E$ using the values of $E_1$ and $T$.

blocks.answer: The synthesized attribute for $E$ is defined as $E.val = E_1.val + T.val$, computing the result of the arithmetic expression.

blocks.markdown: Syntax-directed translation is a method of translating a string into another form by using the parse tree and semantic rules. Each production rule in the grammar is associated with semantic rules that define how to compute attribute values.

blocks.title: Syntax-Directed Translation
blocks.prompt: Describe the syntax-directed translation for the expression $E \rightarrow E_1 + T$ using semantic rules.

steps.latex: Translate the expression into a postfix notation.

steps.text: Define the semantic rule for translation.

blocks.answer: The syntax-directed translation for $E \rightarrow E_1 + T$ is defined by the rule $E.code = E_1.code \; T.code \; '+'$, translating the expression into postfix notation.

blocks.caption: Comparison of Synthesized and Inherited Attributes

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Synthesized attributes flow up the parse tree, while inherited attributes flow down or across the tree.

points: Attribute grammars define how to compute attributes for grammar symbols.
Synthesized attributes are computed from children nodes, while inherited attributes are computed from parent or sibling nodes.
Syntax-directed translation uses semantic rules to guide the translation process of expressions.
